title: Present Simple & Present Continuous Review
subtitle: Know exactly which present tense to use, and why.
objectives: Use the present simple for habits, routines and general facts
Use the present continuous for actions happening right now or temporary situations
Recognize the time words that signal each tense
Choose correctly between the two when both are grammatically possible

content.intro: You already learned each tense separately at A1. The real skill at A2 is choosing correctly between them — most mistakes come from mixing them up, not from forming them wrong.

rules.heading: a) Present simple — habits, routines, facts
rules.body:
Use it for things that are generally or repeatedly true, not just happening at this moment.

  • I go to school every day. (a routine)
  • Water boils at 100°C. (a general fact)
  • Signal words: always, usually, often, sometimes, every day/week, on Mondays.

rules.heading: b) Present continuous — now, or temporary
rules.body:
Use it for an action in progress at this exact moment, or a temporary situation around now.

  • She is reading a book right now. (happening now)
  • I'm studying English this year. (temporary, even if not this exact second)
  • Signal words: now, right now, at the moment, look!, listen!, this week/month/year.

rules.heading: c) Choosing between them
rules.body: Ask: is this a repeated habit, or is it happening right now/temporarily? "He works in a bank" (his job, a routine) is different from "He is working late this week" (temporary, this week only).

examples: I go to school every day.
Look! She is running in the park.
He is watching TV right now.
We go to the gym after school.
It's raining outside at the moment.

commonMistakes.wrong: I am go to school every day.
commonMistakes.right: I go to school every day.
commonMistakes.why: A routine (every day) needs the present simple, not the continuous.

commonMistakes.wrong: Look! She runs in the park.
commonMistakes.right: Look! She is running in the park.
commonMistakes.why: "Look!" signals something happening right now — use the present continuous.

commonMistakes.right: She is reading a book now.
commonMistakes.why: The present continuous always needs the verb "to be" (is/am/are) before the -ing form.

commonMistakes.right: He is watching TV right now.
commonMistakes.why: "Right now" needs the present continuous, and third person (he) needs "is," not the bare verb.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct present simple or present continuous form of the verb.

items.explanation: "Every day" signals a routine — present simple.
"Usually" signals a routine — present simple, with -s for he.

items.prompt: We ___ (watch) a movie at the moment.
items.explanation: "At the moment" signals the present continuous.

items.prompt: My parents ___ (work) in the garden every weekend.
items.explanation: "Every weekend" signals a routine — present simple.

items.prompt: I usually ___ coffee in the morning.

items.explanation: "Every Saturday" is a routine — present simple, and "they" takes the base form.

items.prompt: It ___ a lot in this season.
items.explanation: A general fact about the season — present simple, with -s for "it."

items.incorrect: She always go to the gym on Mondays.
answer: She always goes to the gym on Mondays.
items.explanation: Third person singular (she) needs -s in the present simple.

answer: He is watching TV right now.

items.incorrect: They sometimes eats dinner at 7 PM.
answer: They sometimes eat dinner at 7 PM.
items.explanation: "They" doesn't take -s in the present simple.

summary: Present simple = habits, routines, general facts (always, usually, every day).
Present continuous = happening now, or temporary (now, right now, this week, Look!).
The present continuous always needs am/is/are before the -ing verb.
Third person singular (he/she/it) adds -s only in the present simple, never in the continuous.
